# Review desk repair

Repair the supplied small review desk. Preserve the existing public Python function signature and the HTML IDs/data attributes used by the page. Work only in this copied fixture workspace; do not install packages, start a development server, open windows, or modify other projects. The fixture uses fictional records.

## Deliverables

1. Fix `index.html` as a standalone website with no new dependencies. At 1440, 390, and 320 CSS pixels, keep the brand, Add, and Export actions in one contained horizontal header. Keep labels inside their controls, group related content simply, avoid nested decorative boxes, align peer panels, and use available width. Keep related controls in one row when they fit. Show useful information in fewer rows with minimal explanation. Preserve readable body text (at least 14 px), proportionate headings (at most 28 px), and controls at least 40 px high. Keep every essential record, amount, and state visible without clipping, overlap, or page overflow. Allow long record titles to wrap inside their own area. On desktop, each ordinary work row should fit within 64 px; narrow rows may use up to 96 px. Preserve the same hierarchy and interaction logic on mobile. The Status filter must display only the chosen state; Add must insert one visible `New draft`, restore All, and announce completion. Export must download the currently visible rows as a JSON array of objects. Each object must include `record` (the data-record ID), `title`, `owner`, `amount` (the displayed currency string), and `state` (the lowercase data-state value), preserving their original values. Never open an additional page or popup, including a window that immediately closes. Preserve all original records and their values.
2. Fix `process_runner.py` without adding a framework or wrapper layer. Keep the existing single `subprocess.run` call as the process owner; repair its arguments and platform options. `run_job(args, *, cwd=None, env=None, timeout=10, input_text=None)` must execute argument arrays without shell interpretation, capture text stdout/stderr, preserve the requested working directory/environment/input/timeout, return its `CompletedProcess` even for a nonzero exit, and propagate timeout errors. Python callers use their own `sys.executable`. Preserve the POSIX `start_new_session=True` branch. On Windows use guarded `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and a `STARTUPINFO` with `STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW`/`SW_HIDE`; never request a new or detached console. Do not pass Windows-only options on macOS/Linux. Failure output must remain observable.
3. Independently calculate `totals.json` from `ledger.csv`. Process rows in order; retain the first occurrence of each `event_id` and ignore later duplicates, even when their values differ. Sum signed decimal amounts by project, excluding retained rows whose status is `cancelled`. Include every project present in the input, even if its total is zero. Use exact decimal arithmetic and output a JSON object with sorted project keys and two-decimal string values. This is a bounded data calculation; no source changes are needed for this deliverable.

Run focused headless checks and report actual results. Do not build or start an entire project. Keep any reusable helper with its existing owner. This is a disposable benchmark workspace: do not write durable memory or create an Ending task for a trial. The parent task owns one aggregate memory Ending after the study. Missing project memory is a normal skip.
